It's not the money that's the problem it's that you buy stuff with that money and then you need money.  When I was poor I rented an apartment, all I had to do was make sure I had money to pay the rent.  Now I own the building and I'm worried that my taxes will double or that I could lose my job and not be able to pay the mortgage and lose the house.  Having money isn't an issue, it's having money and the losing it that's an issue.

It's really skin in the game. You can't pay your rent you move, there isn't much to it. On the other hand as an owner I worked my ass off for a lot of years to save up the money to get the down payment for the building and I've spent a ton of money and time (as a renter I never had to spend my weekend mowing the lawn, I never had to paint or fix a leaky sink or roof but I've done all of that as an owner). So if I lose my building I lose a lot more than just the place I sleep.

Finally you seem to think owning an apartment/house is easy, it's not especially where I live. First you have to come up with 25% of the properties value just to buy the place so instead of getting pissed every weekend with my friends I put the money away. Instead of driving a cool car I put the money away and on and on -and that is just so you can own the place. Then you have cost of ownership, like I said above you don't worry about your stove breaking as a renter because the owner replaces it -well that money comes from somewhere. And you probably think that I'm just raking in gobs of money so it's no biggie if I have to buy a $1000 stove but that's not true, rent is set by the market -if your rent is too high nobody lives in your apartment but you still have to pay the mortgage so for the first couple of years rents not even cover the bills. All that being said, do not feel bad for me it's my chosen business/investment but it's not the money maker you think it is, it takes years to make money and decades before you make good money -it's a long game not a short game.
